plugin.md5.title: MD5
plugin.md5.preset.md5-abc: MD5 of “abc” (RFC 1321 test suite, one block)
plugin.md5.preset.md5-empty: MD5 of the empty message (padding only)
plugin.md5.preset.md5-digits: MD5 of the 80 digits from RFC 1321 (two blocks)
plugin.md5.param.encodingHint: Text is hashed as its UTF-8 bytes. Hex lets you enter any bytes, two hex digits per byte.
plugin.md5.param.inputHint: 0 to 128 bytes, which pad to at most three 64-byte blocks. The message may be empty.
plugin.md5.param.detailHint: “Per operation” shows each of the 64 operations of a block. “Per block” runs the whole compression function of a block in one step.
plugin.md5.region.h: Chaining value H (A, B, C, D)
plugin.md5.op.pad: Pad the message to whole blocks
plugin.md5.op.init: Load the chaining value and the block
plugin.md5.op.compress: Run all 64 operations of the block
plugin.md5.value.iv: Initial value A, B, C, D
plugin.md5.step.initial: MD5 turns the {{bytes}}-byte message into a {{bits}}-bit hash value. It pads the message to whole {{blockBits}}-bit blocks, then runs the compression function ({{rounds}} operations in four rounds of 16) once per block, starting from the initial value A, B, C, D. Unlike SHA-1 and SHA-2, MD5 reads and writes its 32-bit words little-endian.
plugin.md5.step.pad_one: Padding (RFC 1321 §3.1–3.2): after the {{bytes}} message bytes ({{bits}} bits) come the byte 80 (the bit 1 and seven zero bits), {{zeros}} zero bytes and the message length in bits as a {{lengthBits}}-bit number, little-endian (lowest byte first). The result is {{count}} block of {{blockBytes}} bytes.
plugin.md5.step.pad_other: Padding (RFC 1321 §3.1–3.2): after the {{bytes}} message bytes ({{bits}} bits) come the byte 80 (the bit 1 and seven zero bits), {{zeros}} zero bytes and the message length in bits as a {{lengthBits}}-bit number, little-endian (lowest byte first). The result is {{count}} blocks of {{blockBytes}} bytes.
plugin.md5.step.initFirst: The initial value (RFC 1321 §3.3) is A, B, C, D = {{h}}. The registers a … d start as these words, and X[0] … X[15] are the 16 words of block 1, read little-endian.
plugin.md5.step.init: Block {{n}} starts from the chaining value H({{prev}}) = {{h}}: a … d ← H({{prev}}), and X[0] … X[15] are the 16 words of block {{n}}, read little-endian.
plugin.md5.step.round: Operation {{i}} of 64 (round {{round}}, function {{fn}}): {{fn}}(b, c, d) = {{f}}. With X[{{k}}] = {{x}} and T[{{i}}] = {{T}}, the sum a + {{fn}}(b, c, d) + X[{{k}}] + T[{{i}}] = {{sum}} (mod 2^32), rotated left by {{s}} bits: {{rotl}}. The new b = b + {{rotl}} = {{b}}; a, c and d take the old values of d, b and c.
plugin.md5.step.compress: Block {{n}}: all {{rounds}} operations in one step. Afterwards a … d = {{vars}}.
plugin.md5.step.feedForward: Feed-forward: H({{n}}) = H({{prev}}) + (a, b, c, d), word by word mod 2^32 = {{h}}. Adding the input back makes the compression function hard to invert.
plugin.md5.step.output: The MD5 hash value is the final chaining value H({{n}}), its four words written little-endian, all {{bits}} bits: {{digest}}.
plugin.md5.term.H: H(b, c, d) = b ⊕ c ⊕ d
plugin.md5.error.encoding: Unknown input format “{{encoding}}”: choose text or hex.
plugin.md5.error.inputLength: The message has {{length}} bytes; at most 128 bytes are allowed.
